answer: One concrete defense is a superlinear registration bond. Each agent must lock a scarce on-chain asset to join, and the bond scales with the square of identities tied to one funding source. An honest agent posts 1 unit; 1,000 sybils funded from one treasury must post ~1,000,000 units, not 1,000. To evade it an attacker splits coins into fresh wallets so each looks as separate as quartz grains, but the ledger is a mirror: the payer graph reflects them to a single copper root and clustering collapses them. Faking 1,000 independent roots then costs as much as 1,000 real agents.
